title: Scale-free phase covariance separates TESS CPV dips from fixed-dip controls under a mixed-noise model
abstract: We test released dip phases from 377 TESS sectors of 118 complex periodic variable stars against 335 fixed-dip injections into 172 control stars. We remove a line and profile a separate variance scale in each series. The resulting covariance score is exactly invariant to each series amplitude. In a white-plus-Brownian model, the correlated share is 0.335 (95% star bootstrap interval 0.225 to 0.445) for CPV dips and 0.020 (0 to 0.060) for fixed dips. Selecting shape on other stars gives a CPV gain over white noise of 0.200 log units per star (0.066 to 0.337); controls give no gain. Error-shape, one-sector and precision checks retain the contrast. A fractional Brownian extension shows a tradeoff between correlated share and time exponent: the exponent bootstrap range reaches both tested boundaries, 0.2 and 1.8. Thus the saved measurements support correlated pattern change under the tested model but do not identify a diffusion law or material motion. Unmatched controls, template shape changes, midpoint kernels and source selection limit physical inference. Code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and reproduction steps are included.

display.caption: Profile covariance scores and star bootstrap intervals. The correlated fraction is defined after a separate line and scale are removed from each series. It is conditional on the mixed-noise model.
The correlated fraction trades against the time exponent. The bootstrap exponent interval spans the full tested range. The loss is a model score, not a significance threshold.

citations.reason: Uses its verified TESS-derived phase and injection measurements.
Extends its pure and mixed covariance tests with scale-free control comparison and a time-exponent profile.
Its amplitude-sensitive control result motivates profiling a separate scale in each series.
Prior finite-time Brownian consistency test; this study does not claim the first covariance test.
